column1: # Edge behaviour across the whole deployed tree: host canonicalisation, live regressions, caching
# per content class, archives (released / in flight), which ErrorDocument answers, header scoping.
# Format: see lib/rows.mjs. Hand-curated; rows marked known-fail= are approved behaviour that is not
# implemented yet (they must fail; an unexpected pass fails the run so the row gets promoted).
# Every row here is unique coverage: raise this with each added row, lower it only with a reviewed deletion.
# Every non-www host that reaches the docroot lands on the final www URL in ONE hop - for grid,
# charts and studio pages, and for archives (whose path must be kept).
# A bare archive root: mod_rewrite leaves it to mod_dir (the archive's .htaccess is in that very
# directory), so the root's <If> redirect adds the slash and canonicalises the host in one hop.
# The blog host maps the grid root's own paths into /blog/ (SE-86), in one hop.
# A slash-less charts/studio URL on www goes straight to the slashed URL in one hop.
# A host the site does not own (an origin health check, a proxy's internal name) is served, not looped.
# http on www is upgraded to https in one hop, keeping path and query (the port-80 rule: proves the
# plain-http listener is seen as port 80).
# A slash-less directory URL on every alias host, over http and https, gets its slash in the SAME
# hop as the canonicalisation (waf-finding.md §20.2) - grid, archive, charts and studio pages. The
# blog host is canonicalised only below an archive, charts and studio (the live grid paths map into
# /blog/), and http on www takes the same single hop.
# An ACME HTTP-01 token has no extension, but it is a file: it is served as it is on www, over http
# and https, never sent to a slashed URL with no token behind it (waf-finding.md §20.1). An alias
# host is still canonicalised, onto the token itself, in one hop.
# Apache matches the rules against the decoded path and re-escapes it in the Location: an encoded
# path keeps its escaping through the host canonicalisation, on every scheme (the hex digits of a
# re-escaped UTF-8 byte come back lower-case). An & needs no escaping, and a %3F would turn into a
# Live regressions from waf-finding.md §2/§3, now fixed: each must land on its final page in one hop.
# Archive redirects stay inside the archive (they used to land on the CURRENT docs).
# The single-hop rewrites are rebased onto the archive, so a slash-less legacy URL skips the add-slash hop.
# Legacy URLs that 404ed in archives while they carried no single-hop rewrites.
# Every redirect is sent Cache-Control: no-cache from the root's always-table rule, which no child
# .htaccess overrides: host swap, add-slash and rule redirects, on every site, live and archived.
# A 304 is a 3xx too, but it refreshes the headers of the copy a cache holds: it keeps that copy's
# long cache rather than turning it into no-cache.
# /charts/{react,angular,vue}/ are landing hubs now (not -> quick-start); javascript still forwards.
# Content-addressed assets: long cache, by hash SHAPE; unhashed /_astro is never long-cached.
# Unhashed static assets: a bounded one-day cache.
# Classes with no rule of their own take the root's default day rather than a browser's heuristic
# lifetime (a Last-Modified and no Cache-Control). An archive keeps its own long cache.
# /example/ is a live demo page: HTML no-cache, never the day-long asset cache.
# Live 404: the root ErrorDocument, revalidated, no agent Link header.
# The asset rules cascade into the subsites through the merged mod_headers config.
# A released grid/charts archive is immutable: everything under it is long-cached.
# A grid archive 404 is the ROOT 404 page (its ErrorDocument is /404.html), so it is not cached.
# A 304 refreshes the cached copy's headers, so it keeps that copy's long cache.
# The charts archive serves its own 404 page, which sits under the archive path and so matches the
# long-cache rule; the root overrides any error status under an archive back to no-cache
# (waf-finding.md §4), so a missing page is never cached as missing.
# A release candidate is patched in flight by scripts/uncached-archives.mjs: no-cache for every
# content class, overriding the archive and hashed-asset caches - grid AND charts.
# Except content-hashed grid assets: the grid archive build keeps its own hashed-asset rule, which
# runs after the root in-flight block (a changed hash is a new URL, so it cannot serve stale).
# Studio archives are never cached, whatever the content class; /studio itself caches normally.
# Each .htaccess is really in effect: its own ErrorDocument answers below it.
# The agent Link header is for successful HTML documents only.
# Markdown twins: content type with charset, Vary: Accept, no Link.
# A page without a twin is left alone: HTML, even for an agent.
# Paths outside the negotiated set do not Vary on Accept (keeps the shared cache key small).
# A compressed response's ETag carries mod_deflate's -gzip suffix; the root strips it from
# If-None-Match so a revalidation is a 304, not the whole body again (If-None-Match outranks
# If-Modified-Since in a browser's request). Root-owned, merged into every subsite and archive.
# The markdown twin and a compressible asset, live and archived.
# Uncompressed responses keep the plain ETag, which always matched.
